title: Health benefits of evidence-based biophilic-designed environments: A review

findings.antecedent: Visual and non-visual connections to nature (direct experience)
findings.consequent: Psychological health and well-being (attention restoration, positive emotions, relaxation, reduced stress)
findings.quote: Several studies found that visual and non-visual con- nections to nature and direct experiences with nature that is made possible by the presence of plants have positively affect psychological health and well-being in outdoor envi- ronments and interior designs

findings.antecedent: Presence of plants in an office (direct experience)
findings.quote: the presence of plants in an office also reduces perceived stress

findings.antecedent: Exposure to nature and sunlight through a window view (direct experience)
findings.quote: in an office setting and a hospital, exposure to nature and sunlight through a window view can improve employee perform- ance and mood
patients are able to recover better from surgery

findings.antecedent: Visual connection to nature and presence of plants (direct experience)
findings.consequent: Cognitive functionality and performance (communication, concentration, productivity)
findings.quote: much of the literature described how a visual connection to nature and the presence of plants in an outdoor/indoor environment... can improve cognitive functionality and perform- ance by increasing communication, concentration, and pro- ductivity

findings.consequent: Sensory perceptions, feelings of well-being, states-of-consciousness, relaxation
findings.quote: being physically present in nature not only could stimulate sensory perceptions and feelings of well-being, but also alters states-of-conscious- ness, especially feelings of relaxation

findings.antecedent: Indirect experiences with nature (biomorphic forms, patterns, materials, natural images)
findings.quote: indirect experiences with nature, such as biomorphic forms and patterns, materials, and natu- ral images that could enhance creativity and productivity

findings.consequent: Worker moods, performance, productivity, and satisfaction
findings.quote: color design in the workplace in- fluences worker moods, performance, productivity, and satisfaction.

findings.consequent: Sense of comfort, naturalness, and restfulness
findings.quote: an interior that is composed of 45% wood imbues a sense of comfort, naturalness, and restfulness

findings.consequent: Sense of mystery, attraction, and preference
findings.quote: a natural-setting space can evoke a sense of mys- tery, attraction, and one's preference

findings.antecedent: High prospect levels and low refuge levels in natural environments (space and place)
findings.quote: Visual connections to nature and exposure to natural envi- ronments with high prospect levels and low refuge levels are restorative

findings.antecedent: Low prospect levels and high refuge levels in natural environments (space and place)
findings.consequent: Negative emotion, physical stress, attention fatigue
findings.quote: exposure to natural environ- ments with low prospect levels and high refuge levels aren't restorative, however, could increase negative emo- tion, physical stress, and attention fatigue

findings.antecedent: Perceived threats in nature-based activities (space and place)
findings.quote: perceived threats in nature-based activities, such as on a mountain, in an alley or forest, or while scuba diving, can lead to feelings of anxiety and fear.

findings.antecedent: Visual and non-visual connections to nature, presence of plants and light (direct experience)
findings.consequent: Physiological stress indicators (stress, heart rate, blood pressure)
findings.quote: Visual and non-visual connections to nature and the presence of plants and light reduces stress, lowers the heart rate, and decreases blood pressure, among other benefits

findings.antecedent: Perceived stimulation from environment and visual-auditory interactions
findings.quote: perceived stimulation from the environment and the visual-auditory interactions thereof can affect a sense of tranquility

findings.consequent: Sense of tranquility and activation of auditory and perception areas in the brain
findings.quote: compared to viewing a freeway, viewing a beach influences a stronger sense of tranquility and activates the connection between the audi- tory and perception areas in the brain.

findings.antecedent: Use of natural analogs (e.g., natural materials)
findings.quote: the use of natural analogs, such as natural materials, can lead to stress reduction.
